Title text 'Figure 2: Radiation correction lowers solar forecast loss'

g.text: Figure 2: Radiation correction lowers solar forecast loss

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Forecasting models train on April 2024–June 2025; their forecasts are scored July 2025–June 2026. Primary training settings; all forecast leads. Only radiation processing changes; comparisons match forecasts and observations. Each row weights its meters and three production training runs equally. A seed sets the random choices in a training run. Loss scores predicted power probabilities against observed power; lower is better. It uses pinball loss, which penalises predicted power thresholds above or below observed power, averaged over 19 probability levels and multiplied by two. The 31 series include demand, solar, wind, biofuel, and battery storage. Frozen capacity is each meter’s 99th percentile of absolute power over the full available history, including readings after the scored period. Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one matched training seed. More negative loss differences favour radiation-corrected inputs. All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.'
